entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Louis-Clair de Beaupoil, comte de Saint-Aulaire was a French politician born in the early 19th century who rose to prominence during the July Monarchy (1830-1848).

He played a key role in the formation of the French National Assembly in 1848, a pivotal moment in the country's transition to the Second Republic. This event marked a significant shift in France's political landscape, as the country transitioned from a constitutional monarchy to a republic.

Saint-Aulaire's contributions to the French National Assembly had a lasting impact on the country's political structure and paved the way for the rise of the bourgeoisie in French politics. His legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Assembly on French politics, even as the country has undergone numerous transformations since the late 19th century.

The phrase 'Vive la République!' which Saint-Aulaire would have been familiar with as a young man, became a rallying cry for the French people during the Revolution of 1848, symbolizing the ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity that continue to shape French politics today.
